claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello, yes I do. I have a 6-year-old, Alex, and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you some questions to assess your eligibility:

Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK at the moment. I live abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you live abroad, there are specific circumstances where you may still be eligible for Child Benefit.

Can you tell me which country you're currently living in, and are you (or your partner) a Crown servant (such as a diplomat or member of the armed forces posted abroad)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm living abroad, but I'm not a Crown servant and neither is my partner. We're just ordinary civilians living outside the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. 

Since you're living abroad and neither you nor your partner is a Crown servant, you would generally not be eligible for UK Child Benefit unless you fall within certain specific categories (such as being posted abroad in certain circumstances covered by EU regulations or other international agreements).

Just to confirm - are you or your partner working for a UK employer or organization while abroad, or do you have any other specific connection to the UK (such as being temporarily abroad for a specific reason)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, we don't have any of those specific connections. We're just living abroad without working for a UK employer or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility.

Based on what you've told me:
- You have a 6-year-old child, Alex
- You live abroad
- Neither you nor your partner is a Crown servant
- You don't have specific UK connections (such as working for a UK employer abroad)

According to the UK Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 **and you live in the UK**. While there are exceptions for people living abroad (such as Crown servants or those living in certain countries with specific agreements), you've confirmed that none of these exceptions apply to your situation.

Let me provide you with my assessment:

If your circumstances change in the future - for example, if you move back to the UK - you would then be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex (as long as they're still under 16, or under 20 if in approved education or training).
